drivingQuestion: With how small a sum may consecrated property be redeemed?
outcomeNote: The mishna records the incident and R' Yosei's variant of it without adjudicating between them.

segments.he: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁהִקְדִּישׁ שָׂדֵהוּ מִפְּנֵי רָעָתָהּ, אָמְרוּ לוֹ: פְּתַח אַתָּה רִאשׁוֹן. אָמַר: הֲרֵי הִיא שֶׁלִּי בְּאִיסָּר. אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: לֹא אָמַר זֶה ״בְּאִיסָּר״, אֶלָּא ״בְּבֵיצָה״, שֶׁהֶקְדֵּשׁ נִפְדֶּה בְּכֶסֶף וּבְשָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף, אָמַר לוֹ: ״הִגַּעְתִּיךָ״, נִמְצָא מַפְסִיד אִיסָּר וְשָׂדֵהוּ לְפָנָיו.
segments.en: There was «an incident involving one who consecrated his field due to its inferior quality.» The treasurers «said to him: You open» the bidding «first. He said:» It is «hereby mine for an issar,» a small sum. «Rabbi Yosei says: That» person «did not say» he would purchase it «for an issar; rather,» he said he would purchase it «for an egg, as consecrated» items «may be redeemed with money or with the equivalent» value of «money.» The treasurer «said to him:» The field «has come into your» possession based on your bid. As «a result, he loses an issar and his field» remains «before him» in his possession.

moves.summary: the outcome: the field passes back to him and he is out only the trivial sum
moves.about: the treasurers direct the man to open the bidding
